title: רב ששת

paragraphs:
1. He was blind, and by his wisdom knew where the king was: Berakhot 58a. Every thirty days he reviewed his learning, saying, “Rejoice, my soul! For you I read Scripture; for you I learned teachings”: Pesahim 68b; see above, R' Hiyya bar Abba. In Menahot 95b, a man hard as iron raised an objection—who? Rav Sheshet. Rashi explains “hard as iron”: sharp to cut through a law like iron. End of quotation. This accords with Ta'anit, first chapter, “Iron sharpens iron”: one piece of iron sharpens another. Tosafot write that “hard as iron” is praise for a Torah scholar. Tosafot rejected Rashi's straightforward explanation: it should have said “a man like iron,” which would suggest sharpness. Since it says “hard as iron,” it is instead praise that he is not easily appeased and does not forgive his insult. They bring proof from Ta'anit, first chapter: “A land whose stones are iron”—read not “its stones,” but “its builders,” meaning Torah scholars. Alternatively, Tosafot's intention may differ from Rashi because Rav Hisda was actually sharper than he, as in Eruvin 67a: Rav Sheshet's whole body trembled at Rav Hisda's dialectic, while Rav Hisda's lips trembled at Rav Sheshet's mastery of teachings. In Zevahim 96b, Rav Yitzhak son of Rav Yehudah frequented Rami bar Hama, left him, and went to Rav Sheshet, and so forth. He explained: when I ask Rami bar Hama something, he resolves it by reasoning; if I find a teaching that refutes it, he says, “If it was taught, it was taught.” When I ask Rav Sheshet, he resolves it from a teaching; if I find a teaching that refutes it, he says, “One teaching against another.” See Rav Sherira Gaon's epistle in Yuhasin: Sinai is preferable to an uprooter of mountains, and Rav Sheshet is Sinai. Thus Rav Hisda and Rami were sharper than Rav Sheshet. How could they call Rav Sheshet “hard as iron” in the sense of sharpness? Therefore Tosafot wrote that “hard as iron” is praise, as above, not sharpness. This is readily understood and correct. I have already written on this in my work, in an exposition.

Rabbah and Rav Yosef sat at the end of Rav Sheshet's discourse—after he finished the exposition—and Rav Sheshet sat and said, and so forth. Rabbah nodded his head, agreeing with him. Rav Yosef said, “Could two great men such as the rabbis err in this matter?”: Eruvin 65b. He said, “May it count to my credit that I fulfilled the commandment of tefillin”: Shabbat 118, end of side b. He fasted every Passover eve, because if he tasted anything in the morning, the meal did not benefit him; he was delicate: Pesahim 108a. He did not dine at the exilarch's house, because his servants were suspected of taking a limb from a living animal. So it was; he also detected meat that had a lesion: Gittin 67b, see there at length. The exilarch's household imprisoned his attendant Rav Gada. Rav Sheshet said, “Gada, come out,” and he came out: Eruvin 11b. Rav Huna sent him to Rav Anan, and he said, “Anan, Anan”; see his entry. He saw a snake in his dream and killed it: Berakhot 57, end of side a. “As the bees do”: Rav Sheshet's translation, Sotah 48b; see Rav Yosef. He handed his maidservant over to the king's army so that they would not take Israel's daughters: see Asheri, Yotze Dofen. He was in Shilhi: Yuhasin, Rav Sherira Gaon's epistle. In responsa ב״ל [unresolved B.L.], part 1, 56c, in Rosh's rulings' name: Rav Sheshet was of Nehardea, where they followed Shmuel. Rav Sheshet was Bava ben Buta's reincarnation: Sheshet by atbash becomes Bava, and he was blind like Bava ben Buta. Sefer ha-Gilgulim, chapter 10; Hesed le-Avraham, spring 5, river 25; Nof Etz Hayyim, branch 3.

Rav Sheshet said, “Rav said this teaching when dozing and lying down”: Yevamot 24b, 91a, 109b; Bava Kamma 47b, 65a, 67b; Niddah 60, beginning of side a; Bekhorot 23b. Responsa Havvot Ya'ir, no. 152, writes that he did not say this disparagingly, but as great praise: given his stature, he could not have erred unless he said it while dozing. He did not say “lying down and dozing.” As Tosafot, Arvei Pesahim, say, there are two kinds of drowsiness: one at the beginning of sleep and one at its end. At its end, even if he errs, since he is gradually awakening he afterward recognizes his mistake and retracts, unlike when he dozes and then lies down, and so forth.

2. His principal teacher was Rav Huna. Sheshet became infertile from attending Huna's lecture; see his entry. Rav Sheshet was Rav Hisda's colleague and greater than he: Ritzba [ריצב״א; conventionally R' Yitzhak ben Avraham], Ba-Kol Me'arevin; see above. ונקרא עולא משגש ארחתיה דאמיה [literally, he is called “Ulla, the confounder of his mother's paths”; grammatical and identity scope unresolved]; see his entry. Rav Nahman was his colleague: Tosafot, Gittin 32a. Rav Yosef was his colleague: Tosafot, Hullin 104b.

3. The halakhah follows Rav Sheshet in prohibitions; see Rav Nahman. Sefer Keritut, Yemot Olam, gate 3, no. 21; Rosh, Lulav va-Aravah, likewise writes this in the name of the geonim's responsa. See Tosafot, Berakhot 42b, 46a; Eruvin 40a, against Rav Nahman; and Tosafot there, 32a. Rav Sheshet versus Rav Hisda: the halakhah follows Rav Sheshet, Eruvin 40a. See Tosafot there: he was greater than Rav Hisda, since Rav Hisda asks Rav Sheshet in several places. See above: Rav Sheshet was Sinai and Rav Hisda an uprooter of mountains, and Sinai is preferable. Responsa Havvot Ya'ir writes that even without this, Rav Sheshet was also very sharp, in Menahot 95b. This follows Rashi's foregoing explanation; Tosafot rejected it, as above.

4. R' Abba bar Kohen. R' Abba bar Zavda was his colleague. R' Avahu said in Rav Sheshet's name: Keritut 24, end of side a. R' Avina asked him: Ketubbot 43a. And R' Adda bar Mattana. R' Adda bar Hama. Rav Aha bar Yaakov was his colleague. Rav Aha bar Hana. Rav Aha bar Huna. Rav Ahadvui bar Ammi asked him. His mother used to nurse Rav Sheshet; Rav Sheshet prayed for him, and he recovered; see his entry. Rav Idi was his attendant. Issi or Ammi bar Natan; see his entry. In R' Elazar ben Azaryah's name, many expositions: Makkot 23a; Eruvin 64, end of side b; Pesahim 118a, several expositions. Rav Sheshet said in R' Elazar's name, in R' Elazar ben Azaryah's name: Yevamot 4a. He said in R' Ammi's name: Sanhedrin, first chapter. He spoke to Ameimar—requires examination; see his entry. R' Assi bar Hama said, “So said Rav Sheshet.” He said in R' Assi's name: Hullin 92b. Rav Gada was his attendant; see above. Giza said to him. Rav Giddel was his colleague. Rav Huna was his teacher. Rav Huna said in Rav Sheshet's name: Pesahim 102b; Menahot 39a. But בשס״ח [provisionally the new Talmud editions; uncollated] corrected it to “Rav Huna bar Yehudah said in Rav Sheshet's name.” Rav Huna bar Rav Yehoshua. Mar Zutra. R' Zeira asked him: Hullin 121b. R' Ze'ira. R' Hagga bar Hana—requires examination. In R' Hiyya the Great's name: Jerusalem Ba-Kol Me'arevin. R' Hiyya bar Avin. Rav Hama applied to him, “Wisdom is good with an inheritance”: Bekhorot 52b. He spoke to Rav Hana bar Bizna. Rav Hisda was his colleague; see above. He asked Rav Sheshet: Eruvin 67a. He spoke to Rav Hisda's interpreter: Zevahim 14a; so בשס״ח [provisionally in the new Talmud editions; uncollated]. “He spoke to Rav Hisda's interpreter; he asked Rav Hisda”: Yoma 49, beginning of side a. He said in R' Yohanan's name: Shabbat 37b. R' Yose bar Natan. Rav Yosef bar Abba. Rav Yosef was his colleague; see above. Rav Yosef bar Hama. Rav Yosef bar Minyomi. R' Yaakov bar Abaye. R' Yitzhak Nappaha expounded, and Rav Sheshet took offense at him. He said, “Tell Rav Yitzhak: Rav Huna already interpreted your teaching.” He said in R' Yirmeyah bar Abba's name: Eruvin 12a; Menahot 39a. Rav Sheshet told him, “Rav stated the teaching like the Samaritans”: Niddah 69a. Rav Nahman was his colleague; see above. Rav Amram. In R' Akiva's name: Sukkah 9a; Beitzah 30b. He said in Rav's name: Jerusalem Avodah Zarah 2:5. Rava said in Rav Sheshet's name: Berakhot, chapter 3, 23b; Helek 92a. He spoke to Rav Sheshet: Bava Metzia 70a, see Rif; Bava Kamma 88a. Rava bar Rav Aha bar Rav Huna. Rabbah: see above. Rabbah bar Ivi. Ravina asked him. Ravina Zuti. Rami bar Hama said; see above. Rav Sheshet objected. Rami bar Hama said, “Here is the man, and here is the refutation.” Rava said, “I see the man; I do not see the refutation.” They sent to R' Abba bar Zavda, who said, “This need not go inside.” Rashi: it need not be brought before the academy members, because none knows how to resolve it. In the geonim's responsa, disparagingly: there is no question. Rava said, “It needs to go into the innermost”: Bava Metzia 16a. Rami bar Hama applied to Rav Sheshet, “David placed the words in his heart”: Shevuot 45b. He spoke to Rav Shmuel bar Abba. Rav Sheshet of Kartiza; see his entry. In Tutai's name.
